full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Shaha J: This application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated 29-3-92 passed by the Court of Settlement, First Court, Dhaka in Case No. 776 of 1987 dismissing the petitioners' case. 

 2. This case was filed by the petitioners under section 7 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. 54 of 1985) against respondent No. 2 Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development, praying for exclusion of the case property in Holding No. 8B/B, 2nd Colony, Mirpur, Dhaka from the 'Kha' list of the abandoned buildings published in the Bangladesh Gazette (Extraordinary) dated 29th September, 1986 under the provisions of the above Ordinance. 

 3. The case of the petitioners, in short, is that the case property was leased out to Ahmed Reza on 7 -9-1961 by the then ADC, Dhaka as "Relief Plot" and since then Ahmed Reza had been possessing the same till his death in November, 1973 on the basis of a registered deed of lease dated 7th September, 1961. After his death his two sons Muktar Ahmed and Iqbal Hussain and two daughters Fahmida Khatun and Akbari Khatun have been possessing the case property as Ahmed Reza's heirs and heiresses and while they were thus the rightful owner in possession of the property in question they sold the same to the petitioners by two separate sale deeds dated 4-10-1978 and since then the petitioners have been owing and possessing the same by constructing 3 semi-pucca structures thereon and letting our the same to monthly bharatias. Their further case is that their vendors and their predecessor-in-interest had all along been in peaceful possession of the case property till they sold the same to them and there was no occasion whatsoever to treat it as an abandoned property at any point of time. The Government did never take over possession of the case property nor did it serve the statutory notice upon the occupiers as required under Article 7(3) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 for surrendering possession before including it in the list of Abandoned Buildings. The further case of the petitioners is that the property in question cannot be included in the list of the abandoned buildings as they are the rightful owners of the same by way of purchase for valuable consideration from Bangladeshi citizens and there was no occasion for the Government to treat it as abandoned property at any point of time under President's Order 16 of 1972 till before 23rd September, 1986 when the respondents arbitrarily enlisted the case property in the list of abandoned buildings. 

 4. The respondents opposed the petitioners case before the Court of Settlement but they did not file any written statement-objection denying the material allegations of the petition. 

 The learned Court of Settlement by its impugned judgment and order dated 29-3-1992 has been pleased to dismiss the petitioners case on findings that there is no evidence on record to prove that Ahmed Reza and his sons and daughters had been living in Bangladesh during and after the War of Liberation and that Ahmed Reza died in Bangladesh after the War of Liberation leaving behind heirs and heiresses. 

 5. Mr. Masood R Sobhan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners, submitted that in view of the fact that allottee Ahmed Reza all along lived in Bangladesh till his death in November, 1973 and owned and possessed the case property all through on payment of "Annual Land Rent" to the Government in his name up to 1974 as evidenced by Annexure-"C" serial and the Burial Certificate Annexure-"T" proving that he died in Bangladesh on 8th November, 1973 and he was duly succeeded by his two sons and two daughters, vendors of the petitioners, there was no occasion for the Government for enlisting the case property in the list of abandoned buildings and, as such, the impugned Gazette Notification is illegal, arbitrary and without lawful authority. Mr. Masood R Sobhan further submitted that having regard to the admitted fact that petitioners have been in possession of the case property through bharatias and the respondents did not serve the statutory notice upon the occupiers asking them to surrender possession of the case property as required by Article 7(3) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 before including the case property in the list of abandoned buildings leading to the impugned Gazette Notification dated 29th September, 1986 it is evident that the property in question cannot be included in the list of abandoned properties-"kha" list and, as such, the purported Gazette Notification dated 29th September, 1986 is illegal, arbitrary, and without any lawful authority. 

 6. The learned Counsel for the petitioners further submitted that the learned Court of Settlement was manifestly wrong in passing the impugned judgment and order totally ignoring the legal incidence of payment of "Annual Land Rent" to the Government in the name of Ahmed Reza for the years of 1973 and 1974, the Joint Survey Report dated 27-6-1979 Annexure-"E" made by two responsible Officers of the Government clearly showing that the case property was never an abandoned property and that Moktar Hussain, Iqbal Hussain, Fahmida Khatun and Akbari Khatun, sons and daughters of allottee Ahmed Reza, duly obtained succession certificate in respect of the properties left by their father Ahmed Reza in Succession Certificate Case No. 768 of 1978 proving that the vendors of the petitioners are the heirs and heiresses of Ahmed Reza and they own the property left by the father Ahmed Reza as citizens of Bangladesh and while being the rightful owners in possession they sold the same to the petitioners by two registered sale deeds dated 4-10-1978 un-mistakeably proving that the case property is not an abandoned property. The learned Counsel further submitted that non-consideration of these material pieces of evidence and the legal aspect of the case on the question of statutory notice under Article 7(3) of Ordnance No. 54 of 1986 have materially affected the impugned decision of the learned Court of Settlement 

 7. The matter was heard by us on 1-3-1997 when none appeared for the respondents and after conclusion of the hearing 6-3-1997 was fixed for delivery of the judgment. On 6-3-1997 when we were about to deliver the judgment Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Additional Attorney-General, appeared before us with Mr. KH Saifuddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, and prayed for a short accommodation for filing an affidavit-in-opposition for contesting the case and his prayer for adjournment was allowed and 12-3-1997 was fixed for hearing the case. On 12-3-1997 we took up the case for hearing at about 12-30 PM but none was present on behalf of the respondents. After hearing Mr. Masud R Sobhan, the learned Counsel for the petitioners, we learnt that he was not served with any copy of affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the respondents. Since there was none to oppose the Rule on behalf of the respondents we started delivering the judgment. After we finished a substantial part of the judgment Mr. KMS Saifuddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, appeared before us and prayed for time for filing an affidavit-in-opposition which, according to him, was under process of preparation, but his prayer at that stage of the proceedings was refused. Mr. Saifuddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, then made over to u the rile of the Ministry of Works, Government of Bangladesh in respect of the case property and urged upon us to consider the materials in the file in deciding the case. Mr. KM Saifuddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney-General only submitted that the file of the Ministry of Works would fully justify the inclusion of the case property in the list of the abandoned properties and he has nothing more to add. 

 8. We went through the file of the Ministry in question and found that it was only on 28th of June, 1979 that for the first time some sporadic efforts were made by an over zealous officer for fishing out a case of abandoned property by bringing the case property within the mischief of abandoned property laws. In pursuance of the said move the Government formed a Joint Survey Team consisting of an Assistant Settlement Officer and an Assistant Engineer to enquire into the matter by conducting a joint survey on the spot for ascertaining the character of the case property and to submit its report to the Superintending Engineer, Abandoned Buildings. The Survey Team submitted its report dated 21st July, 1979 marked Annexure-"E" to the petition and it reads as follows: 

 The above report dated 21st July, 1979 convincingly proves that the case property is not an abandoned property and it does not come within the mischief of an abandoned property as embodied in Article 2 of President's Order 16 of 1972. It appears that the case property was included in the list of "Abandoned Buildings" only on 23rd September, 1986 without any further material on record to justify its inclusion in the list of abandoned properties. 

 10. The petitioners in support of their claim have filed the photo copy of the two registered sale deeds dated 4th October, 1978 as contained in Annexure-"B" and B(1) to the petition. They have also filed the Clearance Certificate and rent receipts showing payment of "Annual Land Rent" to the Government in the name of Ahmed Reza up to 1974. This Annexure-"e" series clearly proves that "Annual Land Rent" for the case property was paid to the Government for the years 1973 and 1974 in the name of allottee Ahmed Reza. The Joint Survey Report submitted by Assistant Settlement Officer and Assistant Engineer dated 21st of July, 1979 Annexure-E proves, beyond doubt, that the case property is not an abandoned property and it does not come within the purview of abandoned property laws. Annexure-I, dated 12th November, 1973 is the Burial Certificate issued by the General Secretary, KalshiJame Mosque, Madrasha, Eidgah and Graveyard Committee showing that Ahmed Reza, the original allottee, had died in Dhaka on 8th November, 1973 and he was buried at the Kalshi Graveyard. The Joint Survey Report Annexure-"E" and the Burial Certificate Annexure- "I", therefore, go unchallenged. All these papers, which remained uncontroverted, unmistakably prove that Ahmed Reza, the original allottee, had been living in Bangladesh till his death on 8th November, 1973 and after his death his 2 sons and 2 daughters, vendors of the petitioners, stepped into his shoes and since then they have been in uninterrupted and peaceful possession of the property in question. While thus being in peaceful possession they sold the case property to the petitioners by two registered sale deeds dated 4th October, 1978. Under such circumstances, we are of the view that the learned Court of Settlement was not at all justified in holding that the case property was rightly declared as an abandoned property on the finding that the petitioners did not produce any oral and documentary evidence showing that Ahmed Reza was living in Bangladesh during and after the War of Liberation. 

 12.It is thus evident that once a property is enlisted as an "Abandoned Property" by observing the legal formalities it becomes conclusive evidence as regards the character of the property in question but the requirement of law is that before a property is enlisted as an "Abandoned Property" notice under Article 7(3) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 must be given to the occupiers. In this case, no notice as required by the Article 7(3) of President's Order 16 1985 appears to have been issued to the occupiers. Admittedly, the case property is still in possession of the petitioners through bharatias. There is absolutely nothing on record to rebut the clear assertions of the petitioners that the statutory notice as required under Article 7(3) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 was never issued by the Government before treating the property as an abandoned property leading to the ultimate publication in the Official Gazette. The impugned judgment of the Court of Settlement does not at all indicate as to whether it at all considered the vital question of the statutory notice as required by law. In the face of the clear assertion by the petitioners that no such statutory notice was ever served upon the occupiers of the case property before treating it as "Abandoned Property and in the absence of any evidence whatsoever to prove to the contrary, it must be held that notice as required under Article 7(3) of the Ordinance was never issued to the occupiers of the case property, leading to the impugned publication in the Official Gazette on 23rd October, 1986. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record the whole exercise appears to be illegal, malafide and without any lawful authority. Since the essential requirements of law as required by President's Order 16 of 1972 and Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 were not complied with before enlisting the case property as an "Abandoned Property" in late September, 1986 it must be held that the respondents acted illegally, arbitrarily and without any lawful authority in making the impugned publication in the Official Gazette treating the case property as an abandoned property. The learned Court of Settlement appears to have totally ignored these vital aspects of the case, the material evidence on record and the law bearing on the subject. Moreover, the learned Court of Settlement also failed to consider the legal incidence of payment of "Annual Land Rent" in the name of allottee Ahmed Reza upto 1974 and the question of uninterrupted and peaceful physical possession of the case property by the original allottee Ahmed Reza and after him by his successors-in-interest, vendors of the petitioners. Failure of the learned Court of Settlement to consider the vital documents in Annexure-"C" series, Annexure-"E" and Annexure "I" to the petition fully supporting the claim of the petitioners must have materially affected the impugned decision. The learned Court of Settlement also failed to take into consideration the Joint Survey Report submitted by two responsible Government Officers clearly certifying that the case property was not an abandoned property and it does not come within the purview of President's Order 16 of 1972. In the context of proved facts the Government has no right to disown the said Joint Survey Report without any fresh convincing materials justifying the cancellation of the said report. The inclusion of the case property in the list of "Abandoned Property" on 23-9-1986 without serving the statutory notice upon the occupiers as required by Article 7(3) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 appears to be wholly illegal and arbitrary. 

 13. The principles of fairness in government action requires that government functionaries must act according to law and must perform their duties in good faith. Public accountability and acceptance demand that government actions must correspond to good conscience and fair play. In the instant case, we are constrained to hold that even minimum fairness was not exhibited in dealing with the case property belonging to a citizen of the country, whose right to property is guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution. The enlisting of the case property in the list of "Abandoned Property", in the circumstances of the case, thus must be held to be illegal, mala fide and without lawful authority. 

 14. We are conscious that the High Court Division in deciding the case is not acting as the court of appeal with the power to lightly interfere with findings of facts arrived at by the learned Court of Settlement. But since the learned Court of Settlement failed to consider material pieces of evidence in Annexures-"C" series, "E" and "T" and the fact of non-service of the statutory notice as required under Article 7(3) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 upon the occupiers of the case property, we are of the opinion that the learned Court of Settlement acted illegally and without jurisdiction in finding that the petitioners have failed to show that the allottee Ahmed Reza and his sons and daughters have been living in Bangladesh during and after the War of Liberation of Bangladesh and that he died in Bangladesh leaving behind legal heirs and heiresses, which are evidently against materials on record. 

 15. In fact, we do not find in the four comers of the record and the file of the concerned Ministry, which we returned to the learned Deputy Attorney-General after our inspection, the existence of any magic wand which whipped up an ordinarily non-enterprising administration to suddenly wake up from its slumber to be galvanised into action for suddenly treating the case property as an abandoned property in late September, 1986. This leads us to conclude that the whole exercise in enlisting the case property as an abandoned property is ill-conceived, malafide and without any lawful authority. 

 16. On consideration of the Annual Rent Receipts-Annexure-"C" series, the Burial Certificate- Annexure- "I", the Joint Survey Report -Annexure- "E" and the succession certificate granted in Case Succession Certificate Case No. 768 of 1978 in favour of the 2 sons and 2 daughters of allottee Ahmed Reza, who are the vendors of the petitioners, we are firmly of the view that there is absolutely no reason to hold and believe that allottee Ahmed Reza was not in Bangladesh when President's Order No. 16 of 1972 came into existence and that his whereabouts were not known and he and after him his successors-in-interest were not possessing the case property, providing the legal basis for treating the case property as an abandoned property, The learned Court of Settlement erred in law in passing the impugned judgment without properly considering the legal effect of all these material pieces of evidence and the same has materially affected the impugned decision. 

 17. For the reasons stated above, we are of the view that the learned Court of Settlement acted illegally and without jurisdiction in dismissing the case of the petitioners on an erroneous view of law and facts, ignoring material pieces of evidence, affecting the ultimate decision of the case and, as such, the same is liable to be set aside in the interest of justice. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute with cost which we assess of Taka 2,000.00 (two thousand) only. The impugned judgment and order dated 29-3-92 passed by the learned Court of Settlement, First Court, Dhaka in Case No. 776 of 1987 are hereby declared to be illegal, arbitrary and without any lawful authority. We further declare that the inclusion of the case property in Holding No. 8B/B, 2nd Colony, Mirpur, Dhaka in the "Kha" list of abandoned properties, (published in the Bangladesh Gazette Extraordinary dated 29th September, 1986), has been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.
